correctness.rationale: After normalizing the equal sides to one and base to x in (0,2), direct median/altitude/inradius formulas reduce the claim to G(x)>=0. On [4/7,(3sqrt(3)-4)/2] the rationalized defect has the correct sign termwise. On the two outer intervals, sign-preserving squaring reduces to S=U-Vsqrt(1+2x^2), with U^2-V^2(1+2x^2)=784(x-1)^2(x-4/7)^2(x+2)^2Q(x). On the left interval Q is strictly increasing by the exact positive Bernstein coefficients of Q'((4/7)u) and Q(4/7)<0, so S<0 with the required original sign. On the right interval the shifted Q has a positive low block and a positive quadratic high block of discriminant -10, while shifted U has all positive coefficients, giving S>=0 and equality only at x=1. The frozen verifier reconstructs these identities exactly in Q(sqrt(3)); it corroborates the symbolic proof rather than replacing it.

originality.rationale: The 2012 primary source states exactly this inequality as Conjecture 4 for all triangles. The submitted theorem resolves the entire nondegenerate isosceles subclass by a global one-variable sign proof. Liu's later 2023 article gives a pointwise lower bound for individual median-minus-altitude differences, but its summed bound is strictly weaker on an explicit isosceles triangle and therefore does not imply the claim. Resultary returned the audited result as the direct exact match and no covering isosceles proof.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased prior proof of the isosceles specialization could exist outside the checked triangle-inequality literature.

value.rationale: This proves an explicitly published open triangle inequality on the complete one-parameter isosceles subclass, including uniqueness of equality, with an exact global certificate rather than numerical evidence. A full symmetry-class resolution of an open conjecture is a motivated mathematical advance even though the scalene case remains open.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased prior proof of the isosceles specialization could exist outside the checked triangle-inequality literature.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate Euclidean isosceles triangle, m_a+m_b+m_c-(h_a+h_b+h_c)>=s-3sqrt(3)r, with equality if and only if the triangle is equilateral.
scientific_limitations: An unindexed or differently phrased prior proof of the isosceles specialization could exist outside the checked triangle-inequality literature.
No claim is made for scalene triangles.
